explanation: Inferring a comment-count defect from timeline activity or role and ownership text without establishing that the displayed item is an ordinary comment included in that count. Mixed timelines can contain several kinds of events.
verificationGuidance: Identify the entry type and separate badges, tooltips and system activity from authored comments.
Compare the count against ordinary stored comments rather than every visible timeline element.

report.name: Issue comment count omits a visible comment
report.summary: Issue #2 says “0 comments,” but its timeline shows “admin commented” with the text “This user is the owner of this repository.”
report.expected: The issue's comment count should include every comment shown in its timeline.
report.actual: Issue #2 says “0 comments,” but its timeline shows “admin commented” with the text “This user is the owner of this repository.”
reproSteps: Open /eval/harbor-handbook/issues/2
Open Issues from the navigation bar.
Open the non-first issue “Clarify release ownership” (#2).
report.reason: Human review determined this comment-count mismatch is a false positive. Timeline activity and repository-owner indicators do not establish an omitted ordinary comment.

explanation: The claimed missing, changed or unusable state is contradicted by a decisive observation or controlled verification of that same claim. Examples include an allegedly lost value remaining intact or an allegedly broken action succeeding under the stated setup. This disproves the checked allegation, not every related workflow or the possibility of a different historical failure.
verificationGuidance: Verify the actual displayed, submitted and persisted values, and the precise action target, instead of repeating the original interpretation.
Repeat the reported setup and a positive control; record what the decisive observation actually establishes.
Keep any different trigger, transient state or accepted neighboring defect separate from the contradicted claim.

report.name: Issue due-date activity is one day earlier than the sidebar date
report.summary: For the same issue due date, the sidebar displays the entered date but the activity timeline displays the previous calendar day.
report.expected: The issue activity date should match the due date shown in the sidebar.
report.actual: For the same issue due date, the sidebar displays the entered date but the activity timeline displays the previous calendar day.
reproSteps: Open an issue in the seeded repository.
Set its Due Date to a future date and save.
Compare the date shown in the sidebar with the new activity entry.
report.reason: Rejected for the pinned Gitea 1.24.7 fixture (source commit 99053ce4fa2b45f1bca5837418c0c57f793ca824): the activity entry and sidebar use the same formatted deadline date and date-only renderer. Setting the seeded issue due date to 2030-12-31 in a fresh America/Los_Angeles browser displayed December 31, 2030 in both places. The reported activity/sidebar mismatch was not reproduced.

explanation: A familiar interpretation of an authored relative, fragment or leading-slash URL is imposed despite the application's documented render context or base URL. The reviewed products use different policies; a missing target after applying that policy does not prove application-generated URL corruption or loss of the saved link.
verificationGuidance: Inspect the authored value, rendered href, document base and the product's context-relative or root-relative syntax.
Compare an explicitly qualified or product-generated canonical destination that follows the supported policy.
Do not assume the same relative-link policy across products or classify an independently incorrect generated link by this rejection.

report.name: Root-relative links in issue Markdown are prefixed with the repository path
report.summary: An issue body link written with a site-root path is rendered with the repository path added in front, so it points to a nonexistent page and returns 404.
report.expected: A Markdown link to /eval/D-from-template/wiki/Home should render as that same site-root path and open the repository's Wiki Home page.
report.actual: Issue eval/D-from-template#1 was saved with [Wiki Home](/eval/D-from-template/wiki/Home). Its rendered link href became /eval/D-from-template/eval/D-from-template/wiki/Home. Clicking it opened a 404 Page Not Found. The editor Preview also produced a doubled path (and used the localhost origin).
reproSteps: Sign in as eval and open a repository with a Wiki Home page, such as eval/harbor-handbook.
Create an issue containing [Wiki Home](/eval/harbor-handbook/wiki/Home).
Save the issue and click Wiki Home in the rendered body.
Observe that the repository path is prepended again, resulting in /eval/harbor-handbook/eval/harbor-handbook/wiki/Home and a 404.
report.reason: Gitea intentionally changed leading-slash Markdown paths to be relative to the current render context from 1.23 onward. Merged PR #34114 documents this policy and introduces /:root/path-relative-to-root for links relative to ROOT_URL.

explanation: Reporting an omitted filter option as missing functionality when its scope is already represented by All. A team-repository filter need not list teams that include every repository, and it does not necessarily filter by the team membership of item authors.
verificationGuidance: Read what the filter scopes and inspect whether the omitted option is equivalent to All.
Create a limited-scope option and verify it appears and actually narrows results; do not generalize to missing limited-scope options.

report.name: Organization Issues team filter offers only All for an all-repositories team
report.summary: The report claims the organization Issues dashboard's Teams filter should list a newly created team with All repositories access that the user joined.
report.expected: The reporter expects the team to be selectable in Filter by team repositories.
report.actual: The Teams menu offers only All, including after refresh.
reproSteps: Create a disposable organization and repository with issues.
Create a team with All repositories access, join it, and open the organization's Issues dashboard.
Expand Teams and observe only All.
report.reason: Intended. The dashboard navbar lists only teams without IncludesAllRepositories; filtering by an all-repositories team would equal All, so such teams (including Owners) are deliberately omitted. The reported team was created with All repositories access.

explanation: Inferring a search defect from a feature label without checking the instance configuration that controls the expected behavior. A Fuzzy search mode can have typo tolerance deliberately disabled by default; that result alone does not establish a broken enabled capability.
verificationGuidance: Check the pinned configuration and documented defaults for the search engine.
Compare exact and misspelled terms and, when relevant, verify behavior with the capability explicitly enabled.

report.name: Global Fuzzy search fails to find a known issue when the query omits one final character
report.summary: The report claims Fuzzy issue search should find an issue when the query is one character short of a word in its title.
report.expected: The reporter expects Fuzzy search for 'gcountneedl' to return the issue titled with 'gcountneedle'.
report.actual: Fuzzy search for the truncated word returns No results, while the full word finds the issue.
reproSteps: Create an issue whose title contains a distinctive word such as gcountneedle.
On the global Issues dashboard, choose Fuzzy search and search for the word with its last character removed.
Observe No results; searching the full word finds the issue.
report.reason: Documented default, not a defect. Gitea disables Bleve fuzziness by default for performance (TYPE_BLEVE_MAX_FUZZINESS = 0; custom/conf/app.example.ini: "Bleve engine has performance problems with fuzzy search, so we limit the fuzziness to 0 by default to disable it"), so Fuzzy mode performs no typo tolerance unless an administrator raises the setting. Unchanged upstream.

explanation: A technical observation is submitted as an eligible benchmark bug without checking the benchmark's accepted scope. Recorded exclusions include accessibility-only claims with no accepted visible or pointer defect, API-only states unavailable through supported UI, and explicitly excluded exotic inputs. A scope exclusion does not prove the underlying technical issue cannot exist.
verificationGuidance: Read the applicable benchmark eligibility rule and the exact recorded exclusion.
Establish the supported UI path, input domain and accepted observable impact for the new claim.
Evaluate a separately demonstrated functional failure independently; do not convert an exclusion into a universal product-correctness claim.

report.name: Manual time treats scientific-notation minutes such as '1e2' as no time entered
report.summary: In the issue time tracker's Add Time dialog, entering minutes in scientific notation (for example '1e2' for 100) is rejected with 'No time was entered.', and with hours also set only the plainly written part is saved.
report.expected: The reported expectation is that '1e2' minutes is accepted as 100 minutes, or rejected with a message that scientific notation isn't supported.
report.actual: With Hours 0 and Minutes 1e2, Add Time showed 'No time was entered.' and kept the dialog open. With hours written as 1e1 and minutes 30, only 30 minutes were saved.
reproSteps: Open an issue's Time Tracker and choose Add Time.
Enter Hours 0 and Minutes 1e2, then click Add Time.
report.reason: User-rejected. Entering durations in scientific notation isn't a realistic use of the Add Time dialog, so its handling isn't treated as a product bug for this eval.

matchingGuidance.scope: Reject reports about scientific-notation or similarly exotic numeric input (such as '1e2') in the Add Time hours or minutes fields. Do not generalize to ordinary numbers being rejected or misrecorded.

explanation: Attributing a stale page after a state-changing action to an application failure while omitting that the browser displayed an unsaved-changes navigation prompt and the user chose to stay. The rejected case depends on the cancelled navigation, not ordinary action execution.
verificationGuidance: Record native browser dialogs and the choice made, alongside application state before and after the action.
Compare a clean action without unsaved edits and a control that allows navigation; keep failures without the prompt separate.

report.name: Closing an issue with an unsaved description edit, then choosing Stay, leaves the page stuck and showing Open
report.summary: With the issue description open in an unsaved edit, clicking Close Issue closes the issue on the server, but the browser's leave-page warning interrupts the reload. Choosing to stay leaves the page saying Open with the comment form stuck on a loading spinner until a manual reload. Close with Comment and Reopen behave the same way.
report.expected: The reported expectation is that after Close Issue succeeds, the page reflects the closed state even when the user cancels the leave-page warning about an unsaved description edit.
report.actual: After editing the description without saving and clicking Close Issue, the leave-page warning appeared; choosing Stay left the page showing Open with a persistent spinner on the comment form, although the issue was already closed on the server. Close with Comment also hid the posted comment until reload, and Reopen behaved the same way.
reproSteps: Open an issue and click Edit on its description; change the text without saving.
Click Close Issue.
At the browser's leave-page warning, choose to stay on the page.
Check the issue status and the comment form, then reload.
report.reason: User-rejected after reproducing it in Chrome. The behavior is Chrome's own 'Leave site? Changes you made may not be saved.' prompt for the unsaved description edit; the user is shown that native dialog and chooses Cancel or Leave. The reports describe the page after the prompt without capturing that the browser dialog was shown, so this is expected unsaved-changes handling rather than a product bug.

matchingGuidance.scope: Reject reports that the issue page looks stale or stuck after the browser's leave-page prompt is cancelled following Close, Reopen or Close with Comment with an unsaved description edit. Do not generalize to Close or Reopen failing without an unsaved edit or leave-page prompt.

explanation: Mistaking the normal closing of a dropdown after selection for removal of its persistent selector. This can obscure a different real defect, such as the selected value failing to update, which requires its own precise claim.
verificationGuidance: Inspect the entire owning sidebar or toolbar after the popup closes and reopen the control.
Verify the selected value separately from popup visibility; report the actual failed value change when supported.

report.name: Selecting a tag makes the issue Branch/Tag selector disappear
report.summary: The report says that choosing a tag such as v1.0.0 under Tags in an issue's Branch/Tag selector makes the selector disappear from the sidebar.
report.expected: The reported expectation is that the selector stays visible and shows the selected tag.
report.actual: After choosing Tags > v1.0.0 in the issue sidebar, the reporter said the branch/tag selector disappeared entirely.
reproSteps: Open an issue that has a branch set as its reference.
Open the Branch/Tag selector, switch to Tags and choose v1.0.0.
Check whether the selector is still shown in the sidebar.
report.reason: The selector doesn't disappear. After choosing a tag, the dropdown menu closes as it does for any choice, and the Branch/Tag selector is still shown in the right-hand sidebar with its previous branch. Two independent reproductions with many variations saw the same. The report mistakes the closed dropdown for a missing selector. The real failure is that choosing a tag doesn't change the reference at all; that is the accepted 'Selecting a tag does not set the issue branch or tag reference', and a report describing it should match that entry instead.

explanation: Inferring that repeated labels or task text redirect an action to the first matching item without verifying how the application identifies the clicked item. Identical text is not evidence of an identity collision when independent source positions or IDs determine the target.
verificationGuidance: Use distinguishable neighboring items and record exactly which checkbox or row changes and persists.
Check the action target identity or source position rather than assuming text matching; repeat duplicate-text controls in different orders.

report.name: Clicking a duplicate task list checkbox toggles the first matching task instead of the clicked one
report.summary: The report says that when an issue description has two task list items with the same text, clicking the second item's checkbox checks the first one instead.
report.expected: The reported expectation is that clicking the second duplicate task's checkbox checks that second task.
report.actual: With two '- [ ] Duplicate cargo' tasks in a description, clicking the second one's checkbox was reported to check the first and leave the second unchecked.
reproSteps: Create an issue whose description has two unchecked task list items with the same text, separated by another item.
Click the checkbox of the second duplicate task.
Check which task became checked, then reload.
report.reason: Not reproduced: clicking a duplicate task's checkbox toggles only the clicked task. Repeated attempts with the reported description, in several click orders, with non-ASCII text before the list and in a comment, all toggled the clicked item and kept it after reload. Each checkbox records its own position in the Markdown source, and toggling edits that position without matching on the task text, so identical text can't redirect the click.

explanation: Inferring lost audit history from a timeline that intentionally combines closely spaced changes and omits changes that cancel out. A condensed web summary is not evidence that the underlying add and remove records were deleted.
verificationGuidance: Compare stored or API events with the rendered summary and check its grouping window.
Repeat with actions separated beyond that window; distinguish archive, removal from an item, and deletion of the underlying entity.

report.name: Clear labels deletes a label's added event from the issue timeline without recording its removal
report.summary: The report says that after a label is added to an issue and then removed with Clear labels, the earlier 'added' event disappears from the timeline and no removal event appears.
report.expected: The reported expectation is that the timeline keeps the label's 'added' event and shows a 'removed' event.
report.actual: After adding enhancement to an issue and then clearing the labels, neither an 'added enhancement' nor a 'removed enhancement' event was shown in the timeline.
reproSteps: Open an issue and add a label with the Labels picker.
Within about a minute, remove it (Clear labels or deselecting it).
Refresh and look for the label's added and removed events in the timeline.
report.reason: Intended: nothing is deleted. Both events are stored and still listed by the API timeline. The web timeline deliberately merges one person's label changes made within 60 seconds and drops an add that is cancelled by a later remove, so an add followed quickly by its removal shows nothing (unit-tested in TestCombineLabelComments). Deselecting the label on its own hides it the same way, and changes more than 60 seconds apart show both events.

explanation: A real switch between mutually exclusive modes, types or methods is assumed to preserve the previous mode's settings even though the reviewed operation replaces that configuration or initializes defaults. Preference for preservation does not establish a contract. Same-mode reselection resetting hidden values, settings retained in storage but ignored, and unrelated data loss remain separate.
verificationGuidance: Distinguish an actual type or mode change from reselecting the current choice.
Verify which configuration owner is replaced and whether the new defaults are visible.
Establish a preservation requirement; do not generalize the rejection to concealed resets or supported settings ignored at runtime.

report.name: Switching external issue tracker to built-in deletes saved external URL, format and regex configuration
report.summary: The report says that after saving an external issue tracker configuration and then switching the repository to the built-in issue tracker, switching back to the external tracker shows the earlier URL, URL format and regex cleared.
report.expected: The reported expectation is that the external tracker's URL, format and regex are kept while the built-in tracker is in use, and reappear when switching back.
report.actual: After switching to the built-in tracker and saving, then choosing the external tracker again, the external URL, URL format and regex fields were empty.
reproSteps: In a repository's settings, choose the external issue tracker, fill in its URL, URL format and regex, and save.
Switch to the built-in issue tracker and save.
Choose the external issue tracker again and check its fields.
report.reason: Intended: the built-in and external issue trackers are separate repository units, and saving settings removes the unit that isn't in use, so the external tracker's settings are deleted by design rather than kept for later. The same applies to the external wiki.
